title: Where Does a Fractal-Seeded Controller Stand? A Simulation Study Positioning a 24-Byte, Estimation-Free Difficulty Controller Against Adaptive Testing, Staircase Rules and a Language Model
description:
🚀 What is New in Version 2.0 (Empirical Positioning & Replication Package)

  • Empirical Positioning & Controller Restructuring: Re-evaluates early conceptual PFP-Core heuristics and replaces them with an empirical simulation battery positioning a 24-byte fractal-seeded adaptive difficulty controller (LearningGate) against Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT, Rasch EAP), fixed-step staircases (=Elo), accelerated PEST, stored-weight matched twins, and frontier Large Language Models (Claude API across 200 learners).
  • Real Data Replay: Mixed-effects logistic regression models calibrated on ASSISTments 2009–2010 (4,163 students, 123 skills) and 2017 (1,709 students, 102 skills) datasets across constant and saturating logarithmic learning trajectories.
  • Verified 24-Byte Seed Equivalence: Demonstrates that the 24-byte seed carrying the multi-scale WERR tripod kernel matches or outperforms its 4-parameter stored-weight twin across 18 of 18 empirical comparisons.
  • Complete Open Replication Suite: Full R, Rcpp, Python, and JavaScript pipelines with strict cross-language floating-point parity (Δ < 10-9) and reproducibility datasets. Legacy v1 artifacts preserved in legacy/ for uninterrupted citation reproducibility.

Open-Science Replication Package & Benchmark Battery (v2.0 • Empirical Study)
Prepared for Flagship Peer-Reviewed AIED Journal Submission
Concept DOI (all versions): 10.5281/zenodo.22999420 • v4.0 Archive: 10.5281/zenodo.23128224
Official Repositories: jesmaat/WerreduR (Canonical Research Repository) • pCwOrM/WerreduR (Engineering Mirror) • pCwOrM/werr (Core Engine)

Abstract

We evaluate an adaptive item-difficulty controller whose step-size policy is procedurally generated from a 24-byte coordinate seed on the boundary of the Mandelbrot set via the WERR fractal kernel. Positioning this estimation-free controller against standard and non-stationary Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT), fixed-step staircases, PEST-type rules, a stored-weight matched twin, and a frontier language model across six synthetic regimes and two empirical ASSISTments datasets, we find that the fractal-seeded rule achieves robust tracking under abrupt ability shifts and fast learning while executing in 0.3 ms per item with zero persistent tensor storage.
